chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) told me, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Ali ibn al-Hazur, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

When the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) approached from Basra, the nobles of the people received him and congratulated him, saying: 'We hope that this authority will remain with you and that no one will ever dispute it with you.'
He said: 'Far off is that – in a speech of his – how could that be when you will be afflicted with the bald?'
They said: 'O Commander of the Believers, and what is the bald?' He said: 'Your wealth will be taken forcibly, and you will not prevent it.'

key_terms.أَشْرَافُ النَّاس: The nobles / elites of the people
key_terms.الصَّلْعَاء: The Bald (a metaphorical term for a period of weakness or loss of wealth/power)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-Sal'aa' (the bald) refer to in the narration of Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (AS) uses the metaphor of 'al-Sal'aa'' (the bald one) to predict the eventual confiscation of wealth by later rulers, a concept often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the Umayyad or Abbasid dynasties. This prediction highlights the transient nature of political power and the economic hardships that would befall the community, contrasting the initial hope for permanent leadership with the reality of forced taxation and loss of autonomy.
